card.name: Theyyam
card.tagline: North Malabar ritual where the performer becomes a god
card.profile: Theyyam (Theyyattam/Kaliyattam) is a ritual worship tradition of North Malabar, Kerala - chiefly Kannur and Kasaragod districts - in which the performer ritually embodies a deity (Kerala Tourism). After extended ritual singing (thottam) and 8-10 hours of preparation, the placement of the sacred headgear (mudi) marks the deity's entry into the performer's body, after which devotees of all castes seek the Theyyam's blessing directly. Some 456 Theyyam types are documented. Performers are predominantly men of Scheduled Caste communities such as Malayan and Vannan; costumes feature towering mudi headgear, deep red-and-black natural face/body painting and skirts of palm fronds. The season runs roughly mid-October to late May (Wikipedia).
card.insight: Theyyam is closely related to Tulu Nadu's Buta Kola - Buta Kola is sometimes described as the parent form from which Theyyam evolved - and is distinct from southern Kerala's Padayani (HandWiki; Kerala Tourism).
